plan.contextChunk: This figure shows four circular archery targets displayed side by side, each labeled with an archer's name (W, X, Y, Z) and marked with four black dots indicating where arrows struck, designed to contrast the independent concepts of precision and accuracy. Archer W's four dots are tightly grouped near the center of the bullseye, representing both high precision and high accuracy. Archer X's four dots form an equally tight cluster but fall entirely outside the target rings to the lower right, illustrating high precision paired with low accuracy. Archer Y's dots are scattered widely across different regions of the target and beyond its outer edge, representing both low precision and low accuracy, while Archer Z shows two dots near the target rings and two far outside, indicating inconsistent and inaccurate performance. This figure introduces precision and accuracy as distinct, independently variable properties of measurement, demonstrating that reproducibility of results does not guarantee closeness to the true value.

interactionPlan.concept: Precision (how tightly repeated measurements agree with each other) and accuracy (how close their center of mass is to the true value) are independent properties, so four archers can occupy all four combinations of the precision × accuracy matrix.
elements: Row of four large square panels with thin light-gray borders, one per archer, each target nearly filling its panel
Target in each panel, exactly three bands as in the source: thick periwinkle-blue outer annulus, white gap ring, solid periwinkle-blue bullseye disk at the center — no additional rings
True-value center point at the bullseye center (shown as a small black crosshair only when metrics are on)
Shots drawn as solid round black dots, sized so four of them read clearly at inline scale
Archer W (PRECISE + ACCURATE): four dots in a tight cluster sitting on/inside the blue bullseye disk
Archer X (PRECISE + INACCURATE): four dots in an equally tight cluster displaced down-and-right, sitting outside the outer annulus

Archer Y (IMPRECISE + ACCURATE): four dots spread far apart but arranged roughly symmetrically around the bullseye (upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right at differing radii) so their centroid lands on the bullseye
Archer Z (IMPRECISE + INACCURATE): four dots spread far apart AND all skewed into the upper-right/right region, so the centroid sits well off the bullseye
Large panel captions beneath each target: 'Archer W', 'Archer X', 'Archer Y', 'Archer Z' (largest type in the figure)
Per-panel classification sub-caption (second-largest type) e.g. 'precise · accurate', 'precise · not accurate', 'not precise · accurate', 'not precise · not accurate'

Metrics overlay per panel: hollow ring marking the shot centroid, dashed circle whose radius is the RMS shot-to-centroid distance (spread = precision), dashed arrow from centroid to bullseye center labeled 'bias'
Numeric readout under each panel when metrics are on: 'spread s = …' and 'bias b = …' in target-radius units
Highlight border + soft tint on the currently focused panel

HTML control strip BELOW the drawing canvas (not inside the SVG): a large 2×2 precision-vs-accuracy table with column headers 'Accurate / Not accurate' and row headers 'Precise / Not precise', each cell naming the archer that lives there (W, X, Y, Z), cells highlighting with the focused archer
HTML drag tray below the canvas containing one oversized draggable black 'new shot' dot with a generous hit area and the label 'Drag a new shot onto any target'

interactions.label: Focus archer
interactions.teaches: Each shot pattern occupies one distinct cell of the precision × accuracy matrix: W precise+accurate, X precise+inaccurate, Y imprecise+accurate, Z imprecise+inaccurate — all four cells are populated, none is redundant.

interactions.label: Show centroid, spread circle and bias arrow
interactions.teaches: Precision and accuracy are two separate measurable numbers: spread = RMS distance of shots from their OWN centroid, accuracy error = distance of that centroid from the bullseye. Archer Y has huge spread yet almost zero bias.

The two ratings respond independently to data: one stray arrow dropped into W's tight group wrecks precision while barely moving the centroid, whereas dragging shots symmetrically outward keeps the centroid on target and only destroys precision.

demo_steps.title: Four archers, four patterns
demo_steps.narration: Each archer fired four arrows at the same target. Look only at the patterns: one tight and centered, one tight and off, one wildly scattered but balanced around the center, one wildly scattered and lopsided.

demo_steps.title: Two rulers, not one
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the metrics. The dashed circle measures spread about the archer's own centroid — that is precision. The dashed arrow from the centroid to the bullseye measures bias — that is accuracy. Accuracy is judged from the centroid, not from each individual arrow.

demo_steps.title: Archer W — precise and accurate
demo_steps.narration: Small dashed circle, almost no bias arrow. The shots agree with one another and with the truth.

demo_steps.title: Archer X — precise but not accurate
demo_steps.narration: The dashed circle is just as small as W's, but the bias arrow is long: a perfectly reproducible result that is systematically wrong.

demo_steps.title: Archer Y — accurate but not precise
demo_steps.narration: The dashed circle is huge, yet the shots straddle the bullseye so their centroid lands on it and the bias arrow nearly vanishes. On average Y is right; on any single shot Y is unreliable.

demo_steps.title: Archer Z — neither
demo_steps.narration: Large dashed circle and a long bias arrow: the shots disagree with each other and their center misses the mark. Random error plus systematic error.

demo_steps.title: Fill the matrix
demo_steps.narration: The 2×2 table below now has an archer in every cell — proof that precision and accuracy vary independently.

demo_steps.title: Add your own shot
demo_steps.narration: Drag the extra dot from the tray onto any target and watch both numbers update: a single outlier inflates the spread while hardly shifting the centroid, showing precision and accuracy responding to different features of the data.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Precision is how well repeated measurements agree with each other; accuracy is how close their average sits to the truth — which is why a tight cluster can be completely wrong (X) and a wild scatter can be right on average (Y).
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: TAXONOMY (must be reproduced exactly): Archer W = precise AND accurate; Archer X = precise, NOT accurate; Archer Y = NOT precise, accurate; Archer Z = NOT precise, NOT accurate. METRIC DEFINITIONS that must produce that classification: let R = radius of the outer blue annulus. centroid = mean of the shot positions. spread s = RMS distance of shots from their own centroid; bias b = distance from centroid to bullseye center. Classify precise when s < 0.20R, accurate when b < 0.20R. Place the dots so W (s≈0.06R, b≈0.05R), X (s≈0.07R, b≈1.1R), Y (s≈0.75R, b≈0.08R — shots deliberately balanced around the center), Z (s≈0.7R, b≈0.8R — all shots skewed to one side) land in those four cells. LAYOUT: four equal square panels in one row across the full width, thin light-gray outline, white interior; the target is drawn large, nearly touching the panel edges. The target has only three bands, matching the source: a thick periwinkle-blue (#8E9BD4) outer annulus, a white gap ring, and a solid periwinkle-blue bullseye disk in the middle. Shots are solid round black dots (no stars, no outlines), radius roughly 1/14 of the target radius. TYPOGRAPHY HIERARCHY: 'Archer W/X/Y/Z' captions are the largest text in the figure (bold, dark gray, clearly legible inline); the 'precise · accurate' sub-captions one step smaller; metric readouts and the 'bias' arrow label smallest but still comfortably readable — never micro-type. Focused panel gets a blue highlight border and pale tint; unfocused panels dim slightly. Metrics overlay: hollow black centroid ring, dashed gray circle of radius s, dashed dark-red arrow from centroid to the black crosshair at the bullseye center labeled 'bias'. CONTROLS OUTSIDE THE SVG CANVAS: beneath the figure place an HTML control strip containing (a) a large 2×2 table, columns 'Accurate | Not accurate', rows 'Precise | Not precise', with W in precise/accurate, X in precise/not-accurate, Y in not-precise/accurate, Z in not-precise/not-accurate, the focused archer's cell highlighted; and (b) a drag tray with one oversized black dot (generous invisible hit area, ~2× its visual radius) labeled 'Drag a new shot onto any target'. Neither the table nor the tray may be drawn inside the four-panel drawing area.

authoredContext:
Consider the results of the archery contest shown in this figure. (a) Which archer is most precise? (b) Which archer is most accurate? (c) Who is both least precise and least accurate?

4 targets are shown each with 4 holes indicating where the arrows hit the targets. Archer W put all 4 arrows closely around the center of the target. Archer X put all 4 arrows in a tight cluster but far to the lower right of the target. Archer Y put all 4 arrows at different corners of the target. All 4 arrows are very far from the center of the target. Archer Z put 2 arrows close to the target and 2 other arrows far outside of the target.

plan.concept: Precision (how tightly repeated measurements cluster) and accuracy (how close they land to the true value) are independent properties — a set of shots can be one, both, or neither.
elements: Four side-by-side rectangular panels with thin dark-gray borders, one per archer

In each panel: concentric target — large white background circle, thick periwinkle-blue outer ring, white gap ring, smaller periwinkle-blue inner ring, white gap, solid periwinkle-blue bullseye center
Center-point marker (true value) at bullseye center of each target, shown as a small crosshair when enabled
Archer W: four black shot dots tightly clustered on/near the bullseye (high precision, high accuracy)
Archer X: four black shot dots tightly clustered below-right and fully outside the outer ring (high precision, low accuracy)
Archer Y: four black shot dots widely scattered — top-right far outside, upper-left, left outside, bottom (low precision, low accuracy)
Archer Z: two dots on the target rings, two far outside (top-right, bottom-right) (low precision, low accuracy)
Panel captions below each target: 'Archer W', 'Archer X', 'Archer Y', 'Archer Z'
Classification callout box showing 'Precision: high/low' and 'Accuracy: high/low' for the selected archer
Numeric readouts in the callout: mean distance of shots from center (accuracy metric) and spread/scatter of shots about their own centroid (precision metric)
Centroid marker (hollow ring) and dashed spread circle drawn around each cluster when metrics are shown
Dashed arrow from cluster centroid to target center labeled 'bias (accuracy error)'
Overlay panel: a single target with all four clusters drawn in distinct colors (W blue, X orange, Y green, Z purple) plus a color legend
Draggable 'new shot' dot in a tray labeled 'Drag a shot onto a target'
2x2 summary legend: precision vs accuracy quadrant labels

interactions.teaches: Each shot pattern maps to a specific combination of precision and accuracy; clicking one panel focuses attention and names that combination explicitly.

interactions.label: Show centroid, spread circle, and bias arrow

interactions.teaches: Precision and accuracy respond to the data, not to a label: dropping one stray shot into a tight cluster destroys precision while barely moving the center, and dragging the whole cluster toward the bullseye restores accuracy without changing spread.

demo_steps.title: Four archers, four patterns
demo_steps.narration: Four archers each fired four arrows at the same target. Compare the patterns before reading any labels: which archer is 'good'?

demo_steps.title: Archer W — precise and accurate
demo_steps.narration: Click Archer W: the shots are tightly grouped AND centered on the bullseye. Repeatable and correct.

demo_steps.title: Archer X — precise but not accurate
demo_steps.narration: Archer X's cluster is just as tight as W's, but it sits entirely off the target. Reproducibility says nothing about correctness — this is systematic error.

demo_steps.title: Measure the two ideas separately
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the centroid, spread circle, and bias arrow. Spread size = precision; arrow length from centroid to center = accuracy. W has small spread and short arrow; X has small spread and long arrow.

demo_steps.title: Archers Y and Z — neither
demo_steps.narration: Y and Z have large spread circles, so poor precision, and their centroids miss the bullseye, so poor accuracy too. Their occasional near-center hit is luck, not skill.

demo_steps.title: Overlay for direct comparison
demo_steps.narration: Stack all four shot sets on one target. Now spread and offset are read at a glance: two tight clusters (one centered, one offset) and two diffuse scatters.

demo_steps.title: Add your own shot
demo_steps.narration: Drag a new shot onto any target and watch the ratings update. One wild arrow ruins Archer W's precision; sliding X's cluster onto the bullseye makes it accurate without changing its precision.

plan.keyInsight: Precision is agreement among your own measurements; accuracy is agreement with the truth — a tight cluster in the wrong place is perfectly precise and completely wrong.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Four equal-width portrait panels in a row, thin dark-gray rectangular outlines, white interiors. Each panel holds a concentric target slightly above center: thick periwinkle-blue (#8E9BD4) outer annulus, white gap, thinner blue inner annulus, white gap, solid blue bullseye disc. Shot marks are small black star-like dots. W: four dots tight around the bullseye edge/center. X: four dots in a tight diamond well below and right of the target, outside all rings. Y: four dots scattered — far top-right outside, upper-left inside outer ring, left outside, bottom outside. Z: one dot on inner ring upper-left, one on inner ring right, one far top-right, one far bottom-right. Captions 'Archer W/X/Y/Z' centered beneath each panel in gray sans-serif. Selected panel gets a highlighted border and a callout above it reading e.g. 'Precision: HIGH · Accuracy: LOW' with green/red chips. Metrics overlay draws a hollow black centroid ring, a dashed circle sized to the shot scatter, and a dashed arrow from centroid to the bullseye center labeled 'bias'. Overlay view shows one enlarged target with clusters color-coded W=blue, X=orange, Y=green, Z=purple plus a small legend. A shot-dot tray sits below the row with the hint 'Drag a shot onto a target'.

Select an archer: Drag the black “new shot” dot from the tray in the figure onto any target to change that archer's ratings. Precision = RMS scatter of an archer's shots about their own centroid. Accuracy = mean distance of shots from the bullseye. Both reported in units of the outer target radius R.

discrepancies: Target ring structure is wrong: the source target is a blue outer annulus, a white gap and a single filled blue bullseye disk, while the generated target adds an extra blue ring/white gap pair (5 concentric bands instead of 3), so each target reads as a different, busier bullseye.

Classification contradicts the source's layout: Archer Y's four shots in the source surround the bullseye (their centroid is essentially on centre), i.e. the classic 'accurate but not precise' case, but the code defines accuracy as mean distance from centre and labels Y as both imprecise AND inaccurate, leaving the 2×2 quadrant cell 'not precise / accurate' empty ('—') and the step-5 narration asserting Y is inaccurate.

Target scale relative to panel is noticeably smaller than the source (source targets nearly fill each panel width); combined with small star markers instead of the source's solid round dots, the panels look sparser and the shot patterns less prominent.

Added content not in the source clutters the figure canvas: a dashed 'drag a shot' tray box and a precision-vs-accuracy quadrant table are drawn inside the figure below the panels, both rendered at a size that is essentially illegible at inline scale.

'Archer W/X/Y/Z' captions are much less prominent than in the source (17px inside a 1200-unit viewBox scales to ~8px on screen), and the top hint line 'Click a target to see its precision and accuracy rating' is similarly tiny.
evaluation.notes: The four-panel archer composition, blue palette and shot patterns are recognizable and the interaction set (step player, toggles, archer select, draggable new shot) is rich and functional, but the target has an extra ring pair, the in-figure tray/quadrant extras are illegible clutter, and the accuracy metric (mean distance rather than centroid offset) misclassifies Archer Y, collapsing the classic 2×2 precision/accuracy taxonomy the source is built to illustrate.
action_items: Redraw the target with exactly the source's bands — outer blue annulus, white gap, filled blue bullseye disk — and enlarge it so it nearly fills each panel as in the source; use solid round black dots for shots rather than 8-point stars.

Define accuracy as the distance of the shot centroid from the bullseye (bias), not the mean per-shot distance, so Archer Y falls into 'accurate but not precise' and all four quadrant cells are populated; update the step narrations accordingly.
Increase font sizes for the 'Archer W/X/Y/Z' captions and any in-figure annotation so they are comfortably readable at inline size, and establish a clear hierarchy (panel captions largest).

Move the drag tray and the precision-vs-accuracy quadrant table out of the drawing canvas (or scale them up substantially) so they no longer add tiny, unreadable clutter beneath the four source panels; enlarge the draggable 'new shot' dot hit area.
plan_action_items: Specify the pedagogical taxonomy explicitly in the plan (W = precise+accurate, X = precise+inaccurate, Y = imprecise+accurate, Z = imprecise+inaccurate) and the metric definitions that reproduce it, so the generated classification matches the source figure's intent.

feedback.rationale: The critic flags a core concept misunderstanding — the accuracy metric and 2×2 precision/accuracy taxonomy are wrong, misclassifying Archer Y — which requires the plan to explicitly define the taxonomy and metrics before implementation fixes matter.

discrepancies: Archer W's cluster is tighter than in the source: generated shots sit at ~0.1R all inside the inner blue disk, whereas in the source the four hits straddle the inner-circle boundary with visibly wider spacing.

The target occupies a slightly smaller fraction of each panel than in the source (source rings nearly touch the panel sides), and the SVG leaves large empty margins above and below the panel row at the default inline size.
Source arrow marks are drawn as slightly star/burst-shaped black blobs; generated uses plain smooth circles (cosmetic, but changes texture at a glance).

evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-composed reproduction of the four-archer precision/accuracy panel figure with correct ring colours and labels, backed by a genuinely rich interaction set (step player, focus buttons, metrics overlay, drag-a-shot, reset) that computes spread and bias correctly; weaknesses are minor — W's cluster is tighter than the source, the targets sit slightly small within their panels, and the secondary metric captions are undersized at inline scale.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items remain and all dimensions score 4-5 with only minor cosmetic deviations, so the figure is good enough to stop iterating.

discrepancies: Archer W's cluster is tighter than in the source: generated shots sit at ~0.1R all inside the inner blue disk, whereas in the source the four hits straddle the inner-circle boundary with visibly wider spacing.

The target occupies a slightly smaller fraction of each panel than in the source (source rings nearly touch the panel sides), and the SVG leaves large empty margins above and below the panel row at the default inline size.
Source arrow marks are drawn as slightly star/burst-shaped black blobs; generated uses plain smooth circles (cosmetic, but changes texture at a glance).
Secondary captions shown at later steps ('precise · accurate', 's = …  b = …') render at roughly 9 px on screen at inline scale — smaller than comfortable next to the 12–13 px archer names.
